committeeQuestion.question: At which point does evidence change hands in a decision-critical process, and who can reject or correct it?
committeeQuestion.why: An AI comparison, custody arrangement or record-handling process can produce a result without showing whether the next operator received enough evidence and authority to challenge it.
committeeQuestion.evidence: The original instruction, source record, changes made, system comparison, exception disposition, receiving owner and the final decision record.

committeeQuestions.question: If a fund or adviser changes a crypto-custody arrangement, who controls access, recovery and the records needed to prove what happened?
committeeQuestions.why: The SEC has proposed additional custody pathways, including limited self-custody and state trust-company custodians. The proposal is not yet a rule, but it sharpens the choices and safeguards firms may need to assess.
committeeQuestions.evidence: Current custody mandates, key and account access, segregation, recovery procedures, reconciliations, incident responsibilities and any proposed-state readiness assessment.

committeeQuestions.question: Can we show who safeguards sensitive records through use, storage, transfer and disposal?
committeeQuestions.why: The Irish DPC’s published summary describes a specific case involving paper health records and confidential waste, followed by orders to complete DPIAs and implement controls.
committeeQuestions.evidence: Record locations, authorised access, retention and disposal procedures, DPIA actions, control owners, inspection evidence and closure records.

judgement.title: The control must survive the hand-off.
judgement.editorialAngle: The critical control is the evidence, judgement and authority carried from one operator or custodian to the next.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 15 traced dependencies that could change an outcome and asked who could halt them. This edition follows the control inside the hand-off: what the next operator receives, what they can challenge, and who resolves a mismatch.
judgement.observation: OpenAI reports Chatham checks AI-assisted transaction comparisons against experienced reviewers. The SEC has proposed new crypto-custody pathways; the UK NCA reports a confiscation order after conviction; Ireland’s DPC requires DPIAs and controls after paper-record failings; and CISA has added two exploited vulnerabilities.
judgement.executiveJudgement: Controls can fail between steps. If the receiving person or system cannot see the authorised instruction, the comparison and any exception, they cannot challenge or own the final record.
judgement.implication: Replay one high-impact record from instruction to decision. Collect the evidence each step receives and ask the next owner to resolve a mismatch. Use the first gap you find to assign one specific control fix.

weeklyReadout.heading: A control is only as strong as its hand-off.
steps: Evidence is moving between people, systems and custodians.
A record can be complete at one point and unusable at the next.
Replay one record from authority to final decision.
Find who can reject or correct a mismatch.

topSignals.title: Chatham’s AI trade validation remains under expert review
topSignals.label: AI-assisted control
topSignals.why: The application compares transaction terms and flags discrepancies, but the supplier reports that the customer is still checking results against experienced reviewers before expanding automation.

topSignals.title: CISA adds two known-exploited vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog
topSignals.label: Known-exploited vulnerabilities
topSignals.why: CISA’s catalog additions are based on active exploitation. The immediate decision is whether the affected products exist in the firm’s own estate and what remediation or mitigation is recorded.
topSignals.source: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency · Public authority · 2026-10-02

topSignals.title: UK NCA secures a £290,000 confiscation order after a people-smuggling conviction
topSignals.label: Post-conviction proceeds recovery
topSignals.why: The NCA describes a court confiscation order and restrictions on bank accounts and business interests in one case, illustrating how proceeds-of-crime work can continue after conviction.

topSignals.title: SEC proposes new crypto custody paths for advisers and funds
topSignals.label: Proposed custody framework
topSignals.why: The SEC proposal could add self-custody in defined circumstances and state trust-company custodians for advisers and regulated funds. It remains a proposal, so firms can assess their custody choices without treating it as current law.
topSignals.source: US Securities and Exchange Commission · Regulator · 2026-10-01

topSignals.title: Irish DPC orders DPIAs and controls after children’s paper-record failings
topSignals.label: Sensitive-record handling
topSignals.why: The DPC summary links physical custody and confidential-waste handling to GDPR security duties and required DPIAs and controls. Its full decision is still to be published.
